g.text: Two families of I/O channels
FILE-LIKE
the other end is a device, with data that stays
P
I/O channel
file
The data is there before and after the process.
It has a size, and any byte can be read again:
the channel keeps a position, and it can be moved.
A read gets what is there, or the end; it does not wait
for somebody to write.
a file on a disk, a block device, a directory
this lecture, parts 05 and 06
SOCKET-LIKE
the other end is a process, and data passes once
P1
I/O channel
P2
The data exists only between a write and a read.
No size, no position: what was read is gone,
and nothing can be read twice.
A read waits until the other end writes,
and ends when the other end closes.
a pipe, a FIFO, a Unix socket, a network socket
lectures 10 and 11
A terminal sits in between: it is a device, and it behaves like the second family, because a person is at the other end.
